study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., The Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to identify the optimal approach for normative modeling of brain morphometry through systematic empirical benchmarking, quantifying accuracy across algorithms and identifying parameters that optimize performance. It also articulates the purpose of applying normative modeling, including methodological robustness and potential research/clinical utility.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We aimed to identify the optimal approach for normative modelling of brain morphometric data through systematic empirical benchmarking, by quantifying the accuracy of different algorithms and identifying parameters that optimised model performance." ... "This model can inform about the biological and behavioural implications of deviations from typical age-related neuroanatomical changes and support future study designs."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For the new reference models, the paper describes eligibility criteria (healthy individuals without psychiatric, medical, neurological morbidity or cognitive impairment; baseline scans only) and image quality/data completeness standards (ENIGMA QC pipelines, ABCD QC flags, Qoala-T, Euler number). It also reports the final sample size (37,407) and provides procedures for outlier removal. However, detailed reasons for exclusion at the participant level are not comprehensively enumerated across all datasets.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Data were further selected to include high-quality neuroimaging measures ... from participants who did not have psychiatric, medical, and neurological morbidity and cognitive impairment at the time of scanning. Only scans acquired at baseline were included..."; "For samples participating in the ENIGMA Lifespan Working Group ... pipelines were applied to 18,787 individuals ... ABCD ... applied to 3,116 ... for the remainder ... quality assessed using Qoala-T ... As an additional assessment of image quality, we calculated the Euler number (EN)..."; "Sex-specific subsamples ... were mean-centred after extreme values, defined as any values greater than 1.5×IQR, in each subset were identified and removed."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Ge2024.pdf.md – Samples/Methods (lines ~19–27, 40–52); Ge2024_sup6.pdf.md – S1/S2 Quality assessment (lines ~91–97)

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are central (sex-specific models; age as explanatory variable with non-linear polynomials). Multi-site effects are addressed via two strategies: treating site as a random factor and applying ComBat-GAM harmonization; the study compares both. Global neuroimaging covariates (ICV, mean cortical thickness, total surface area) are included as linear covariates.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "All models were sex-specific... trained with five-fold cross-validation ... with age being the only explanatory variable" (for initial selection); "The potential effect of site on performance was addressed both by handling site as a random factor and by site-harmonisation using ComBat-GAM and then comparing the resulting models."; "optimised with non-linear polynomials for age and linear effects of global measures as covariates."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data sources are described as 87 datasets spanning multiple regions and consortia, with specific datasets, scanner details, and access information enumerated in Supplementary Table S1.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We collated de-identified data from 87 datasets from Europe, Australia, the USA, South Africa, and east Asia..."; "Supplementary Table S1. Datasets included in the model optimization sample with access information" (site, scanner, FreeSurfer version, N, age).

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Not applicable as models are built from secondary/aggregated datasets (87 datasets).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and pipelines are described: morphometric feature extraction from T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer standard pipelines; quality control via ENIGMA protocols, ABCD qc flag, Qoala-T, and Euler number calculation. Site harmonization via ComBat-GAM was evaluated. QC/outlier removal procedures are reported.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Morphometric feature extraction from whole-brain T1-weighted images was implemented with the standard pipelines in the FreeSurfer image..."; "quality assessment followed the ENIGMA consortium pipeline ... applied to 18,787 individuals ... ABCD ... fsqc_qc ... 3,116 ... Qoala-T tool for 15,504 ... As an additional assessment of image quality, we calculated the Euler number (EN)..."; "The potential effect of site ... handled ... by site-harmonisation using ComBat-GAM"; "extreme values ... >1.5×IQR ... removed".
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: Ge2024.pdf.md – Methods (lines ~23–27, 40–52, 120–140); Ge2024_sup6.pdf.md – S2 Quality assessment (lines ~91–97)

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study uses a clear data partitioning strategy: sex-specific 80/20 train/test splits stratified by site and age, with five-fold cross-validation within training sets and evaluation on held-out test sets.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Sex-specific subsamples ... split into a training subset (80%) and a test subset (20%), through stratified randomisation by scanning site and age. ... The models were trained with five-fold cross-validation (5F-CV) in the corresponding sex-specific training subset ... Model parameters were tested in the corresponding sex-specific test subset."
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: Ge2024.pdf.md – Data preparation and Algorithm selection (lines ~45–73)

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An external application to healthy individuals is presented as a longitudinal stability check in SLIM and QTAB healthy cohorts, suggesting external application beyond the development sample. However, this is framed as stability rather than a formal external validation of model fit metrics in an independent healthy dataset, and it is unclear whether these datasets overlap with the 87 original datasets.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We illustrate the stability of the optimised MFPR-derived models over an average interval of 2 years in data from the SLIM and QTAB study samples using ... exemplars."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approaches are comprehensively described: eight candidate algorithms (OLSR, BLR, GAMLSS, LMS, GPR, WBLR, HBR, MFPR) and their implementations in R and Python, with MFPR selected as optimal. Key settings include non-linear fractional polynomials for age and linear global measure covariates; software libraries (mfp in R; PCNtoolkit in Python) are named.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "The data ... were analysed with the following algorithms: (1) OLSR ... (2) BLR ... (3) GAMLSS ... (4) LMS ... (5) GPR ... (6) WBLR ... (7) HBR ... (8) MFPR, implemented with the mfp package in R ..."; "The multivariate fractional polynomial regression (MFPR) emerged as the preferred algorithm, optimised with non-linear polynomials for age and linear effects of global measures as covariates."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is quantitatively assessed with MAE, RMSE, explained variance, and CPU time, across training/test splits and age bins; sample size effects and performance plateau are reported.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The MAE ... served as the main measure of model performance, supplemented by the RMSE ... and by explained variance."; "The MAE and RMSE values of the optimised MFPR-derived ... models plateaued at a sample size of approximately 3000 participants."; "robustness of the model accuracy across all age groups".

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: The study reports the partitioning strategy (80% training, 20% testing) and stratification by site and age. However, explicit sample sizes and demographic summaries for each partition are not fully tabulated in the text.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "Sex-specific subsamples ... split into a training subset (80%) and a test subset (20%), through stratified randomisation by scanning site and age."
